title: The Builder–Critic Loop
subtitle: A task queue that stores the future, a builder that ends with evidence, and a critic's gauntlet that alone grants verified
throughline: one task's journey from the top of the queue, through the builder's claim and the critic's gauntlet, to verified

chapters.title: The Queue Is the Future
chapters.blurb: Git stores the past; .eforest stores the future — a task queue generated from frontmatter, gated by a project state machine.

steps.title: The Queue Is the Future
steps.coverSubtitle: Git stores the past. .eforest stores what happens next.
steps.spoken: Every repository stores its past. This one also stores its future — and an agent loop that turns one into the other.
steps.displayNarration: `.git` stores history. **`.eforest/`** stores *the future of what we are building and the proof of what we have built* — the queue, the loop, the evidence.

steps.title: A task is a folder
steps.spoken: A task is a folder, and its readme opens with frontmatter: an id, a priority, a status, and the tasks it depends on. That little block of metadata is the single source of truth for what the task is and where it stands.
steps.displayNarration: A task is a **folder** — `.eforest/tasks/epic-*/E*-T*/` — whose `readme.md` frontmatter carries `id`, `priority`, `status`, `depends_on`.

steps.title: The queue is generated
steps.spoken: A small python tool walks every task folder, parses that frontmatter, sorts by priority, and regenerates the queue file. Nobody edits the queue by hand — if the board and the tree ever disagree, the tool warns out loud.
steps.displayNarration: `tools/build_queue.py` parses every readme's frontmatter and **regenerates `QUEUE.md`** — sorted by `priority`, *never edited by hand*. A folder-name/frontmatter `id` mismatch is a warning.

steps.title: Implemented is not done
steps.spoken: Each task carries one of five markers: pending, in progress, implemented, refuted, or verified. And here is the tell of the whole system: implemented is not done. Implemented means awaiting adversarial verification.
steps.displayNarration: Status markers: `[ ]` pending · `[~]` in-progress · **`[?]` implemented — awaiting adversarial verification** · `[!]` refuted · `[x]` verified.

steps.title: The project state machine
steps.spoken: The project itself is a state machine too: building, complete, paused, or invalid loop. The loop refuses to run unless the project says building — and invalid loop is a loud stop, never a silent retry.
steps.displayNarration: `.eforest/project.json` holds the project state: `building` · `complete` · `paused` · **`invalid_loop`** — a *loud stop* when the loop can't converge honestly.

steps.title: One task in flight
steps.spoken: From the queue, exactly one task is in flight at a time: the top eligible one, whose dependencies are all verified. No new task may start until the current gate clears.
steps.displayNarration: **One task in flight.** The builder takes the *top eligible* task — every `depends_on` already `verified`; no new task starts until the current gate clears.

steps.title: The one rule
steps.spoken: And everything that follows serves one rule. A builder being satisfied is a claim. A deterministic recording of the run that satisfied them is evidence. No task reaches verified on claims.
steps.displayNarration: **The one rule:** a builder being satisfied is a *claim*; a deterministic recording of the run is *evidence*. No task reaches `verified` on claims.

chapters.title: The Builder's Claim
chapters.blurb: One task, gates in ascending cost, and two layers of recorded evidence — the builder ends with a claim, not a merge.

steps.title: The Builder's Claim
steps.coverSubtitle: Gates in ascending cost, evidence in two layers, and a claim instead of a merge
steps.spoken: The builder takes the task at the top of the queue. What it hands back is not a merge — it is a claim, with the evidence to interrogate it.
steps.displayNarration: The **builder** implements exactly one task and submits three things: *the diff, a claim, and recorded evidence* of the final happy run.

steps.title: Pick the top task
steps.spoken: A builder session picks the top eligible task and gets a private workshop: the task's own work folder, gitignored scratch space where it can probe and self-validate without limit.
steps.displayNarration: The builder self-validates freely inside the task's own **`work/`** folder — *gitignored scratch*, ephemeral runs, no limit.

steps.title: Gates in ascending cost
steps.spoken: Before any claim, the change passes the build gates in ascending cost: format check and lint, then typecheck, then tests, then build. All of them must pass — they are Makefile targets with real exit codes, not a checklist.
steps.displayNarration: Build gates, *ascending cost*: `pnpm format:check && pnpm lint` → `pnpm typecheck` → `pnpm test` → `pnpm build` — encoded as Makefile recipes (`_v-gates`).

steps.title: Stream-layer evidence
steps.spoken: Then the builder records evidence, in two layers. The first is always there: a dumped event log replayed to a state digest. Same log twice, same digest — determinism is the proof, and the dump lands in the task's committed evidence folder.
steps.displayNarration: **Stream layer** (always): a dumped event log replayed to a **state digest** — `ef replay --digest`, canonical JSON, SHA-256. Durable artifacts go in the task's `evidence/`.

steps.title: Browser-layer evidence
steps.spoken: The second layer covers anything a user can reach: a full Replay browser recording of the final happy run, uploaded and cited by URL. Not trust me, I checked — here is the session where it worked, in full.
steps.displayNarration:
**Browser layer**: a **Replay recording** of the final happy run, cited by *point link* — `app.replay.io/recording/?point=

&time=` — never committed, always interrogable.

steps.title: Write the claim
steps.spoken: Finally the builder appends an entry to the task's verification log: the commit, the exact commands, the evidence paths and recording URL. Silence about an evidence layer is forbidden — absence must be declared, with a reason and a mitigation.
steps.displayNarration: The claim lands in the readme's **Verification log**: commit, exact commands, evidence paths, recording URL. *Absence must be declared* — `Replay: N/A (<reason>) + mitigation`.

steps.title: Status: implemented
steps.spoken: The builder flips the task to implemented and stops. It cannot go further: the status verified does not belong to the one who did the work. That belongs to a stranger.
steps.displayNarration: Status flips to **`implemented`** — and the builder is done. Only a *fresh critic session* may ever set `verified`.

chapters.title: The Critic's Gauntlet
chapters.blurb: A fresh session attacks the claim — cold clones, falsification, coverage, sabotage — and a judge issues the verdict.

steps.title: The Critic's Gauntlet
steps.coverSubtitle: A task is done only when a hostile critic fails to break it
steps.spoken: Now the claim meets its adversary. The doctrine is one line: a task is done only when a hostile critic fails to break it.
steps.displayNarration: **The critic runbook:** *a task is done only when a hostile critic fails to break it.* A fresh session — never the one that implemented.

steps.title: The evidence gate
steps.spoken: Before reading a line of code, the critic checks the claim itself. If it cites no recording URL and no event log digest, the verdict is needs evidence, immediately. Absence declared is legitimate; silence is not.
steps.displayNarration: **The evidence gate:** no Replay URL *and* no event-log digest → verdict `needs-evidence` *before reading a line of code*.

steps.title: Cold-clone first
steps.spoken: First rule of the loop: never verify the implementer's working tree. The critic clones the committed head into a scratch directory with the environment scrubbed — node options, node env, npm config, all cleared. A green there is a real green.
steps.displayNarration: **Cold-clone first** — `tools/verify/cold_clone.sh` clones pristine HEAD into a scratch dir with `NODE_OPTIONS` / `NODE_ENV` / `npm_config_*` *scrubbed*. Never the builder's tree.

steps.title: Falsify and audit coverage
steps.spoken: Then the attack proper, from two directions at once. Falsification hunts for one point where the program contradicts the claim — interrogating the actual Replay recording through the Replay MCP, citing point links. Sufficiency holds the evidence against the diff: changed code the evidence never exercised is either unproven or dead.
steps.displayNarration: Two attack directions: **falsification** (one point where the program contradicts the claim — via the **Replay MCP**, cited by point link) and **sufficiency** (*unexecuted diff is unproven or dead*).

steps.title: Sabotage: mutants must go red
steps.spoken: The critic also runs the task's own attack angles with fresh inputs, invents at least one novel attack, and then mutation tests the armor itself: break one acceptance criterion in a scratch branch, and the verify target must turn red. A mutant that stays green refutes the check, not just the code.
steps.displayNarration: **Mutation-test the armor:** break an acceptance criterion in a scratch branch — `verify-E<n>-T<nn>` must go **red**. *A mutant that stays green is a refutation of the check.*

steps.title: The judge cross-examines
steps.spoken: The critics are report only — they cannot fix code or flip a status. Their findings flow to a judge in yet another fresh session. And because a refutation is also a claim, each finding must survive cross examination before it counts.
steps.displayNarration: Critics are **report-only**. Findings flow to a fresh **judge** — and *a refutation is also a claim*: each finding is cross-examined before it counts.

steps.title: The verdict
steps.spoken: The judge issues one of three verdicts: verified, refuted, or needs evidence. Verified is terminal — only this session may grant it. Refuted sends the task back to the builder with the findings as new context.
steps.displayNarration: **`VERDICT: verified | refuted | needs-evidence`** — appended to the Verification log; the status flips and the queue regenerates. Only the critic side may set `verified`.

steps.title: Refuted past the budget
steps.spoken: And if reworks keep failing, the loop does not push the task through. Past the retry budget, the whole project flips to invalid loop and halts, loudly, pending a human. Honest failure beats a dishonest green.
steps.displayNarration: Refuted past the **retry budget** → the project flips to **`invalid_loop`** and *halts pending a human* — never a dishonestly green board.

chapters.title: The Spine That Verifies Itself
chapters.blurb: Verified tasks deposit permanent verify targets; self-check hunts green-washing; sensitivity probes prove the checks can go red.

steps.title: The Spine That Verifies Itself
steps.coverSubtitle: Every verified task makes the next one harder to fake
steps.spoken: One last question remains: who verifies the verifier? The loop's answer is a spine of checks that tests itself — and gets stricter with every task it passes.
steps.displayNarration: The **verify spine**: per-task `make` targets, a self-check that audits them, and sensitivity probes that prove the checks can still fail.

steps.title: Acceptance as make targets
steps.spoken: Every task's acceptance criteria are encoded as a make verify target — commands with real exit codes. Verify list maps each target to its task, and the targets outlive the task: they become the permanent regression armor.
steps.displayNarration: Each task's acceptance criteria live in **`make verify-E<n>-T<nn>`** — *commands with real exit codes* (`Makefile`), mapped by `make verify-list`.

steps.title: Verify the verifier
steps.spoken: Self check audits the auditors: every implemented or verified task must have a verify target, and no verify path may contain a green washing escape — no or true, no exit zero, no swallowed failures. Silence is forbidden.
steps.displayNarration: **`self_check.sh`** enforces: every `implemented`/`verified` task has a target, and no verify path hides `|| true`, `; exit 0`, `continue-on-error` — *green-washing escapes fail the build*.

steps.title: Prove the checks can fail
steps.spoken: But a checker that never fires is just decoration. So sensitivity probes plant real escapes — a swallowed failure in the makefile, a malformed task — and demand that self check goes red. Every plant that passes is itself a failure.
steps.displayNarration: **`self_check_sensitivity.sh`** plants real escapes (`|| true` in a Makefile recipe, malformed frontmatter) and asserts `self_check.sh` goes **red** — `expect_red`, per plant.

steps.title: The suite compounds
steps.spoken: All the per-task targets compose into verify all, the standing regression suite every epic runs before touching the core. This is the compounding: each verified task deposits its checks at the front of the pipeline, so the next claim faces a stricter wall.
steps.displayNarration: **`make verify-all`** composes every promoted target into the *standing regression suite* — each verified task makes the pipeline **stricter** for the next.

steps.title: The queue advances
steps.spoken: A verified verdict regenerates the queue, and the next task unlocks. Twenty one of a hundred and one so far — every one of them interrogated, none of them taken on faith.
steps.displayNarration: `verified` → `python3 tools/build_queue.py` regenerates **`QUEUE.md`** and the next task unlocks — *21 / 101 verified, none on faith*.

steps.title: The whole loop
steps.spoken: That is the whole machine. A queue that stores the future. A builder that ends with a claim and a recording. A gauntlet of fresh critics and a judge who alone grants verified. And a spine of checks that proves it can still say no. Evidence, not trust — all the way down.
steps.displayNarration: **Recap:** queue → builder → claim + evidence → critic gauntlet → verdict → stricter spine → next task. *Evidence, not trust — all the way down.*
